name: long_incident
state:
Incident log, payments-api, 2026-10-14.
08:52 UTC deploy 2026.10.14-3 rolled out to eu-west (canary 10%).
09:03 error rate on POST /v1/charges rises from 0.2% to 4.1% in the canary; p99 latency 2.3 s (baseline 410 ms).
09:05 auto-rollback is disabled for this service since the migration last week; nobody is paged because the alert threshold is 5%.
09:11 canary promoted to 50% by the release train as scheduled.
09:14 error rate 11.8%, mostly 'card_declined' with reason 'issuer_timeout'; card networks report no incident.
09:16 on-call (M. Okafor) paged by a customer escalation from a large merchant; starts investigating.
09:24 diff of the release shows the HTTP client timeout to the issuer gateway changed from 8 s to 800 ms (a units bug in the new config loader: milliseconds read as seconds / 10).
09:27 manual rollback started; 09:33 rollback complete, error rate back to 0.3%.
09:40 about 18,400 charges failed between 09:03 and 09:33; merchants were told to retry; no double charges found.
10:15 postmortem scheduled; action items: re-enable auto-rollback, lower the alert threshold to 2%, add a unit test for the config loader, add canary analysis to the release train.

root_cause.instructions: What was the root cause of the incident?

criteria.network: a failure of the card networks
criteria.timeout_config: a wrong timeout value from a units bug in the config loader

customer_impact.instructions: How severe was the customer impact?

process_gap.instructions: Did a process or tooling gap make the incident last longer?
